choices.text: Agree - equal areas mean the shapes are identical
Disagree - congruence needs every matching side and angle to be equal
Agree - but only if the perimeters match too

questions.feedback: That equal-area answer is the one to unlearn: Two shapes with the same area are congruent. Reteach point: Equal area says nothing about shape: congruence needs every matching side and angle.
questions.misconception: Two shapes with the same area are congruent.
questions.prompt: Shape X and shape Y both have area 24 cm². A classmate says they must be congruent. Which response is correct?

questions.feedback: Scene s1 fixes this: three matching pairs of sides force the triangles into exactly the same shape, which is the SSS test.
questions.prompt: State the congruence test used when all three pairs of matching sides of two triangles are equal.

questions.feedback: Scene s3: volumes scale by the cube of the length ratio, 2³ = 8, so the model volume is 8 × 15 = 120 cm³.
questions.prompt: A model is built at length scale factor 2 from the original. The original has volume 15 cm³. What is the model's volume?

questions.feedback: Scene s6: by the alternate segment theorem, the angle between the tangent and the chord equals the angle in the alternate segment, so it is also 48°.
questions.prompt: A tangent touches a circle at P and a chord runs from P into the circle. The angle between the tangent and the chord is 48°. State the size of the angle in the alternate segment.
